<section class="section s-white" id="causes" aria-labelledby="why-title"><div class="wrap">
<div class="head"><span class="eyebrow">Causes we see most</span><h2 id="why-title">Why drains block in Sydney</h2><p class="lead">Six causes account for nearly every blocked drain we are called to. Each one looks different from the fixture, and each one needs a different job underneath.</p></div>
<div class="causes">
<div class="cause "><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-tree"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Tree roots</h3><p>Roots are the most common reason a Sydney drain blocks more than once. Older suburbs sit on clay earthenware pipe laid in short lengths, and every joint is a seam that can open slightly as the ground moves. Roots find the moisture, work into the gap and keep growing inside the pipe until they hold back everything that passes.</p><p>Cutting the roots out clears the line, but the opening they came through is still there. That is why the camera goes in afterwards, and why the fix is sometimes <a href="/services/pipe-relining/">pipe relining</a> rather than another clear.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is timing. A blockage that returns every few months, often worse after rain, is almost always roots.</p></div></div>
<div class="cause " id="kitchen"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-utensils"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Fat, grease and food waste</h3><p>Cooking fat goes down warm and sets hard further along the line where the pipe is cooler. Each wash adds another layer until the bore narrows enough to catch everything else. Kitchen lines in units and food premises build up sooner than most, because the same stretch of pipe takes everything from several sinks.</p><p>Grease responds well to <a href="/services/high-pressure-water-jetter/">high pressure drain jetting</a>, which scours the pipe wall back rather than punching a hole through the middle of the build-up.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is a kitchen sink that drains slowly and gurgles, while the bathroom is unaffected.</p></div></div>
<div class="cause " id="bathroom"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-shower"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Hair, soap and bathroom build-up</h3><p>Bathroom wastes block from the fixture outwards. Hair binds with soap scum into a mat that sits in the trap or just past it, and because it builds slowly most people only notice when water starts standing in the base of the shower.</p><p>These are usually short jobs. The line is cleared mechanically and checked, and if the same waste keeps blocking the camera goes in to find out whether something further along is holding it up.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is one fixture affected while everything else in the house runs normally.</p></div></div>
<div class="cause "><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-wind"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Foreign objects</h3><p>Wet wipes are the main offender, including the ones sold as flushable. They do not break down the way toilet paper does, so they snag on any roughness in the pipe and collect everything behind them. Nappies, sanitary products, cotton buds and children’s toys account for most of the rest.</p><p>Objects usually cause a sudden blockage rather than a gradual one, and they often need to be removed rather than pushed through, which is why a camera is worth running before anything is forced.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is a drain that was completely normal yesterday and is completely blocked today.</p></div></div>
<div class="cause is-struct"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-trowel"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Collapsed, cracked or misaligned pipe</h3><p>Clay pipe becomes brittle with age, and ground movement, heavy vehicles over a driveway or nearby excavation can crack it or pull a joint out of line. Once a section drops or bellies, waste stops running cleanly through it and solids settle at the low point.</p><p>No amount of clearing fixes this. The pipe has to be repaired, either by <a href="/services/pipe-relining/">relining the damaged section</a> from the inside or, where the line has lost its shape altogether, by <a href="/services/pipe-replacement/">replacing it</a>.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is a line that clears easily and then blocks again within weeks, in the same place every time.</p></div></div>
<div class="cause is-struct"><span class="cz"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-cloud-rain"></use></svg></span><div><h3>Silt, leaves and stormwater debris</h3><p>Stormwater is a separate system from sewer, and it blocks differently. Leaves, silt and roof grit wash into pits and downpipes and settle wherever the fall flattens out. Most of the year the line copes, then the first heavy storm arrives and the water has nowhere to go.</p><p>Clearing the pit is only half of it. If water still backs up afterwards, the problem sits further down the <a href="/services/blocked-stormwater-drain-sydney/">stormwater line</a> and needs to be found before the next downpour.</p><p class="tell"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-question"></use></svg> The giveaway is a drain that only misbehaves when it rains hard.</p></div></div>
</div></div></section>
<section class="section s-light" aria-labelledby="how"><div class="wrap">
<div class="head"><span class="eyebrow">Camera first, then clear</span><h2 id="how">How we clear a blocked drain</h2><p class="lead">Four steps, in this order, every time. The camera comes first because everything after it depends on what the camera finds.</p></div>
<div class="steps2">
<div class="st2"><h3>Find the cause first</h3><p>A drain camera goes down the line before anything else. It shows what is blocking it, how far along it sits and whether the pipe itself is sound. Guessing at this stage is how the same blockage comes back.</p><img class="shot" src="/uploads/best-method-for-blocked-drain-clearing.jpg" width="640" height="480" alt="Drainer running an inspection camera into a drain to find what is causing the blockage before anything is cleared" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></div>
<div class="st2"><h3>Match the method to the blockage</h3><p>Roots and solid build-up are cut out with an <a href="/services/electric-eel-drain-cleaning/">electric eel</a>. Grease and silt are scoured off the pipe wall with <a href="/services/high-pressure-water-jetter/">high pressure jetting</a>. The camera decides which, not habit.</p><img class="shot" src="/uploads/electric-eel-drain-cleaning-sydney.jpg" width="640" height="480" alt="Sydney plumber feeding an electric eel drain machine into a blocked drain at a Sydney property" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></div>
<div class="st2"><h3>Clear the line and prove it</h3><p>The blockage is removed and the line is run clear, then tested with water so you can see it taking flow properly rather than taking our word for it.</p><img class="shot" src="/uploads/high-pressure-water-jetting-sydney.jpg" width="640" height="480" alt="High pressure water jetting nozzle scouring the inside of a blocked drain pipe on a Sydney job" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></div>
<div class="st2"><h3>Show you what caused it</h3><p>The camera goes back in after the clear. If the pipe is damaged you see the footage and get the repair options. If it was simply build-up, you get told that too, and nothing further is sold to you.</p><img class="shot" src="/uploads/cctv-drain-camera-footage-on-monitor-sydney.jpg" width="640" height="480" alt="CCTV drain camera footage on a monitor showing the inside of a cleared Sydney drain pipe" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></div>

<span class="co-ic"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-warning"></use></svg></span><div>
<h3>When clearing is not the answer</h3>
<p>If a drain has blocked repeatedly in the same spot, the problem is usually the pipe rather than what is passing through it. Roots entering an open joint and a cracked or fallen section both behave the same way: the line clears easily, runs well for a few weeks, then blocks again.</p>
<p>At that point another clear is money spent on the symptom. <a href="/services/pipe-relining/">Relining</a> seals the damaged section from the inside without digging, and <a href="/services/pipe-replacement/">replacement</a> is for lines that have lost their shape altogether. The camera footage is what decides between them, and you see it before anything is quoted.</p>

Clearing is done through an existing access point and nothing is excavated.</p><p>If the pipe turns out to be damaged, <a href="/services/pipe-relining/">relining</a> is trenchless and is the first option considered precisely because it avoids digging. <details class="faq"><summary><span class="fq-mark"><svg class="ico" aria-hidden="true"><use href="#i-chev-down"></use></svg></span>Why does my drain keep blocking after it has been cleared?</summary><div class="fq-body"><p>Because clearing removes the blockage, not the reason for it. The two usual reasons are tree roots entering through an open joint and a section of pipe that has cracked or dropped.</p><p>If a line has blocked more than once in a year, the useful next step is a <a href="/services/cctv-drain-inspection/">camera inspection</a> rather than another clear.</p></div></details>

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to clear a blocked drain in Sydney?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blocked drains are cleared from $69, and there is no call-out fee, so nothing is charged for coming out to look at it. The final figure depends on where the blockage sits and what is causing it. A bathroom waste full of hair is a short job. A root mass in the main line under a driveway is not. You are given the price before any work starts and nothing proceeds until you agree to it.

Most single blockages are cleared in the same visit. Where the camera finds a damaged pipe rather than a blockage, the line is cleared so the property can be used, and the repair is quoted separately so you can decide on it in your own time.

mainEntity.name: Will you dig up my garden?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not to clear a blockage. Clearing is done through an existing access point and nothing is excavated. If the pipe turns out to be damaged, relining is trenchless and is the first option considered precisely because it avoids digging. Excavation is only recommended where a line has collapsed or fallen so badly that a liner cannot restore it.

mainEntity.name: Why does my drain keep blocking after it has been cleared?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because clearing removes the blockage, not the reason for it. The two usual reasons are tree roots entering through an open joint and a section of pipe that has cracked or dropped. If a line has blocked more than once in a year, the useful next step is a camera inspection rather than another clear.
